newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PAPER UNION SEES PRESSURE FOR BRANCH TALKS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PAPER UNION SEES PRESSURE FOR BRANCH TALKS.

text.p: The Finnish paper workers' union said in a statement on Monday that it was under strong pressure to hold branch-level incomes settlement talks for a new pay deal from February 1998 onwards.
The union would decide its stance on the form of the coming incomes settlement at its representatives meeting starting June 9.

Before the next round of collective bargaining talks, issues like the training insurance scheme and the conditions for EMU-membership important for paper workers must be solved, union chairman Jarmo Lahteenmaki said in the statement.
Before any pay talks could start, the results of a study of the effects on earnings of the current two-year incomes agreement should be reviewed, the union said, noting that this was due in November.
"But due to many branch-specific problems, the paper union is under strong pressure for a branch-level round (of pay talks)," it said.
For example the use of non-union labour was one such problem, it said.
Earlier, metal workers' union chairman Per-Erik Lundh in a speech at the spring council meeting of his union, called for a two-year broad centralised incomes settlement.
Lundh said the deal should cover all branches to make sure inflation and interest rates remained low.
